newsitem.title: MONACO: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV JOINS GROWING LIST OF OUSTED SEEDS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV JOINS GROWING LIST OF OUSTED SEEDS.

text.p: Third seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov joined a growing list of early casualties at the Monte Carlo Open on Wednesday when he was ousted by Norway's Christian Ruud.
The Russian French Open champion, who had a first round bye, was beaten 6-4 2-6 6-4 in the second round.
Kafelnikov's defeat followed the exit of leading seeds Pete Sampras and Thomas Muster, but was not so surprising since he has only played, and lost, two matches this year.
It left Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands the highest remaining seed in the draw at number four.
After two days of upsets - seven seeds bid an early farewell to the tournament on Wednesday - only six seeds will be left in the third round.

American Jim Courier, Swiss Marc Rosset, Swede Thomas Enqvist, South Affrican Wayne Ferreira and Spaniards Alberto Berasategui and Felix Mantilla were the other big names to lose in the second round on Wednesday.
Sampras, Muster and Germany's Boris Becker crashed out on Tuesday.
Consequently, Krajicek, impressive conqueror of Germany's Michael Stich, Chile's Marcelo Rios and Spain's Albert Costa were left with the best chance of lifting the title.

Krajicek, who had just flown back from Japan after winning in Tokyo last week, was amazingly quick to adapt to the surface. His 6-3 6-0 demolition of Stich, losing finalist in the French Open last year, led him to believe in his chances this season on clay.

"I feel pretty good going into the French Open this season. I think I was one of the best players at the French last year. If only I had not felt so tired in the end of my match against Yevgeny (Kafelnikov)," he said.
Kafelnikov beat him in the quarter-finals in Paris on his way to the title.
In the third round, Krajicek will meet another big server, Australian Mark Philipoussis, who was too strong for former French Open champion Courier.
The American, seeded eighth, struggled to return the Australian's serve and failed to impose his pace in his 7-5 7-5 loss. A break at the end of each set was enough for Philippoussis to get through.
Fresh from winning in Barcelona on Monday, Albert Costa crushed Czech Slava Dosedel in straight sets and will face Rios in a re-match of last year's semifinal here.
Costa leads a strong squad of six Spaniards left in the draw.

Former French Open champion Sergi Bruguera, Alex Corretja, winner in Estoril two weeks go, qualifiers Carlos Costa and Emilo Alvarez will also be bidding to repeat the feat achieved in Estoril and Barcelona, when the four players left in the semifinals were all Spanish.
